If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) in the last 5 days, reduce forecasted decline in early horizon (1–7 days) by 5–10% to avoid overcorrection.  
If sentiment is consistently negative (≤-0.33) in the last 5 days, increase forecasted rise in mid horizon (8–15 days) by 5–10% to counteract pessimism.  
When sentiment swings sharply from positive to negative within 3 days, shift forecast downward by 3–5% in late horizon (16–30 days) to reflect sentiment reversal.  
If sentiment is neutral (0.00–0.33) across last 7 days, apply a 2–4% downward bias to forecast in mid horizon to avoid overconfidence in trend continuation.  
If sentiment is positive but recent prices are trending downward, reduce forecasted peak in late horizon by 5–8% to align with price momentum.  
If sentiment is negative but recent prices are trending upward, increase forecasted trough in early horizon by 3–7% to reflect sentiment-driven reversal.
